resolved_by: Sentencing Commission Amendment 822 (effective Nov. 1, 2023), which struck the inchoate-offense language from Application Note 1 and added USSG § 4B1.2(d) to the Guideline text, expressly responding to the circuit conflict
issue: Does a prior conviction for an attempt or conspiracy to commit a controlled substance offense count as a 'controlled substance offense' under USSG § 4B1.2(b) for career offender purposes, given that Application Note 1 is not entitled to Stinson deference after Kisor?

sides.position: Inchoate offenses (attempt, conspiracy) are included in the controlled substance offense definition under § 4B1.2(b), following Application Note 1 and binding Eighth Circuit precedent (Merritt; Mendoza-Figueroa)
cases: United States v. Cupples, 105 F.4th 1096 (8th Cir. 2024)

sides.position: Application Note 1's inclusion of inchoate offenses is not entitled to deference after Kisor v. Wilkie, so inchoate offenses are not included in the plain language of § 4B1.2(b)

this_court: does not decide. The panel affirmed under binding Eighth Circuit precedent (Merritt; Mendoza-Figueroa) and did not reach the merits of the conflict, noting the Commission's later amendment
quote: We recently considered these conflicting circuit authorities but concluded our panels are still bound by Mendoz-Figueroa “until it is overruled by the Court sitting en banc.”
cite: United States v. Scott Cupples, 105 F.4th 1096 (8th Cir. 2024)
